title: U.S. House · Arizona's 1st District
area: Northeast Phoenix metro area, including Scottsdale, Paradise Valley, Cave Creek, Fountain Hills, and part of north Mesa.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Republican David Schweikert, who had held the seat since 2011, did not seek re-election and instead ran for governor of Arizona. Amish Shah won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.5% of the vote over Marlene Galán-Woods, Jonathan Treble, and Rick McCartney. Jay Feely won the Republican primary with 49.8% over Joseph Chaplik and John Trobough. Monica Alponte won the Libertarian primary. Two write-in candidates, Gage Thunder (no party preference) and Dev Gupta (independent), are also on the general-election ballot. Cook Political Report rated the district R+1; in 2024 Schweikert defeated Shah 51.9%-48.1% while Donald Trump carried the district 51.1%-48.0%.

candidates.name: Amish Shah
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.5% of the vote

summary.text: Amish Shah is an emergency-medicine physician and the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He served in the Arizona House of Representatives from 2019 to 2024, representing District 24 and later District 5, and unsuccessfully challenged incumbent Rep. David Schweikert for this seat in 2024.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois. Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Northwestern University in 1997, an M.D. from Northwestern University in 2001, and a master's in public health from the University of California, Berkeley in 2003.
Worked as an attending physician with Mayo Clinic, Dignity Health, and IASIS Healthcare, and as chief medical officer of Urgent Consult.
Served in the Arizona House of Representatives, District 24 (2019-2023) and District 5 (2023-2024).
Was the Democratic nominee against incumbent Rep. David Schweikert in the 2024 general election, losing 51.9%-48.1%.

priorities.text: Says he has 'a track record of being an independent voice working across party lines to put Arizona families first while standing up to extremist attacks on abortion and voting rights.'
priorities.quote: focused on increasing teacher pay, supporting small businesses, and improving public health and safety. He had more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade. ... [He] has a track record of being an independent voice working across party lines to put Arizona families first while standing up to extremist attacks on abortion and voting rights.

priorities.text: Campaign material highlights increasing teacher pay and supporting small businesses as priorities from his state legislative record.

record.text: As an Arizona state representative, served on the House Appropriations Committee and House Health and Human Services Committee (2023-2024 session), and on the Health and Human Services and Regulatory Affairs Committees in earlier sessions.

candidates.name: Jay Feely
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 49.8% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Former NFL kicker and CBS sports analyst

summary.text: Jay Feely is a former NFL placekicker (2001-2014) and CBS football analyst, and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. As of the July 2026 primary he had raised $2.53 million to Amish Shah's $1.83 million.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Michigan in 1998.
Played as a kicker for six NFL teams from 2001 to 2014, then worked as an NFL analyst for CBS.

priorities.text: Describes his approach as bringing the same 'unwavering commitment to having a positive impact' from his football and broadcasting career to public service, without detailing specific legislative proposals on his campaign site as of this research.
priorities.quote: never backed down from hard work or hesitated to stand up for what he knows is right. From the pressure-filled moments on the football field to the bright lights of the broadcast booth, and his deep involvement in the community through his charitable work, Jay has approached every chapter of his life with the same unwavering commitment to having a positive impact.

summary.text: Monica Alponte is the Libertarian nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District. She completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey ahead of the 2026 election.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona, 2026

researchNotes: This is an open, battleground seat. Candidate campaign websites for Shah and Feely did not render usable text content in this environment (JavaScript-rendered pages), so positions were drawn from quoted material on Ballotpedia's 2026 battleground-election summary rather than direct campaign-site issue pages; specific issue-by-issue positions could not be independently confirmed and are left out per the research standard rather than inferred. Monica Alponte (Libertarian nominee) completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, but her responses were not fetched within this research session's time budget; her entry is marked minimal. Two write-in candidates (Gage Thunder, no party preference; Dev Gupta, independent) are on the general-election ballot per Ballotpedia but have negligible public footprint and are not given full entries. Federal key votes and FEC totals are not applicable since neither major candidate is a sitting member of Congress; campaign finance totals mentioned in context come from Ballotpedia's own reporting, not verified FEC filings.
